The correct minimum fractional revival time is t* = 2π/p, which none of the three solutions gives.

**Graph structure.** The units of Z_{2p} are the odd residues not divisible by p. So x ~ y exactly when x and y have opposite parity and y − x ≠ p. Since p is odd, x + p has opposite parity to x. The graph is therefore K_{p,p} minus a perfect matching, where the matching joins each x to its antipode x + p.

**Spectrum.** Order the vertices so that A = σ_x ⊗ B with B = J − I, where J is the all-ones p×p matrix. B has eigenvalue p−1 on the all-ones vector and −1 on its orthogonal complement. The eigenvalues of A are therefore ±(p−1) and ±1.

**Evolution.** Since σ_x² = I,

e^{-itA} = I⊗cos(tB) − i σ_x⊗sin(tB).

Write cos(tB) = cos t·(I − J/p) + cos((p−1)t)·J/p and sin(tB) = −sin t·(I − J/p) + sin((p−1)t)·J/p.

**Fractional revival between x and its antipode x'.** The state U(t)e_x must be supported only on {e_x, e_{x'}}. This requires the J/p terms to vanish in both blocks:

- cos((p−1)t) = cos t
- sin((p−1)t) = −sin t

Together these give (p−1)t ≡ −t (mod 2π), so pt ≡ 0 (mod 2π). The other option, (p−1)t ≡ t, forces sin t = 0, and that gives only perfect revival or no revival, not fractional revival.

The smallest positive solution is t* = 2π/p. At this time U(t)e_x = cos t · e_x + i sin t · e_{x'}, a genuine fractional revival between antipodal vertices.

**Checking the solutions.**
- Solution 1 gives 2π/(p−1). This is wrong, because it treats the walk as returning when the largest eigenvalue's phase returns, and ignores the fractional-revival conditions.
- Solution 2 gives π. This is wrong, and its justification is unsupported.
- Solution 3 gives p. This is wrong, because it confuses a graph distance with a time.

CHOICE: NONE
